examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Y-Intercepts of a Hyperbola
examples.worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}7{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2} & =28 \\ 7{y}^{2}-5(0)^{2} & =28 \\ 7{y}^{2} & =28 \\ {y}^{2} & =4 \\ y & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercepts are $(0,\pm 2).$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(y+3)^{2}-3{x}^{2} & =21 \\ 2(0+3)^{2}-3{x}^{2} & =21 \\ 2(3)^{2}-3{x}^{2} & =21 \\ 2(9)-3{x}^{2} & =21 \\ 18-3{x}^{2} & =21 \\ -3{x}^{2} & =3 \\ {x}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

We cannot take the square root of a negative number. Therefore, the equation has no real solutions. So, there are no $x$-intercepts.
